subject: RFI: Version backporting, provenance attestations, and pinning workflow
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pinebridge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Version backporting, provenance attestations, and pinning workflow

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Pinebridge is consolidating a set of vendor attestations around model provenance and backporting to meet our internal change-control and audit requirements. We have a few targeted questions about how Redwood handles version pinning, backports/security patches, and provenance artifacts for open models. Please see the attached spreadsheet (Pinebridge_RFI_v3.xlsx) — the relevant rows are 12-24, but I pasted the three key questions below to keep responses short: 

- For an upstream model update (e.g., bug fix, tokenizer change), what is Redwood's policy for offering a backported binary (security/bug fix) for a pinned version? What SLAs or timelines do you provide for backports vs. major version upgrades?
- What provenance artifacts do you produce per catalog entry and per served model instance? We are specifically looking for commit hashes, source repo links, training data snapshots (if provided), license files, and a cryptographic timestamp.
- Describe the pinning workflow for customers: who can request a repin, how are requests validated, and how do you ensure rollforward/rollback safety during a pinned rollout?

Additionally, we want to know if Redwood provides a signed attestation (PDF) we can store in our compliance system after an initial onboarding.

Could you respond by EOD Wednesday PT? If helpful, we can do a short sync.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Senior Procurement Analyst
Pinebridge Financial

Attachments: Pinebridge_RFI_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 72KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pinebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Version backporting, provenance attestations, and pinning workflow

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (product policy) and Sean (platform ops) so we can provide concrete artifacts and an operational SLA. High-level answers below; we'll attach a provenance matrix and a brief pinning playbook for your records.

1) Backports vs. major upgrades:
- Security/backport policy: For any critical security fixes (CVSS >=7.0) that affect a released model, we produce a backported inference artifact within 10 business days for Dedicated and Private customers; hosted customers receive a notification and automatic fallback options unless they request pinned binaries. For non-critical bug fixes, we evaluate severity and schedule backports on a 30-day cadence.
- SLA tiers: Dedicated (contracted) customers have an explicit backport SLA and priority triage; Hosted customers can request backports via support but are generally routed to compatible minor-version variants.

2) Provenance artifacts produced per catalog entry and per deployed instance:
- Catalog entry artifacts: source repo URL, canonical commit hash, license file (text), model card, declared training data provenance summary (high-level descriptions, third-party attributions), and timestamped build metadata.
- Deployed instance artifacts: served binary checksum (SHA256), build recipe, docker/packaging image digest, GPU execution config, and a signed provenance token (timestamped) when requested.
- We provide a downloadable ZIP for each pinned release that includes the above; see attached redwood_provenance_matrix_v1.xlsx for mapping to your RFI rows.

3) Pinning workflow and governance:
- Who can request: An org's Admin or the primary contact on the contract can open a 'pin' request. Requests are validated by matching the requested commit/hash to our internal catalog and by a short security review (automated + ops checklist) before a pin is approved.
- Approval path: Customer request -> automated compatibility checks -> ops validation (non-blocking for non-security changes) -> schedule for pin.
- Rollforward/rollback safety: We create canary rollout windows for pinned binaries, and maintain a rollback artifact produced in the original pin workflow. Reverts are automated for Dedicated/Private where requested; on hosted instances we provide immediate fallback to the nearest compatible variant.

4) Signed attestation:
- We can produce a signed attestation PDF (HSM-backed signature) that includes commit hash, SHA digests, license citation, and a timestamp; this is available for on-boarding packages and for Contract/Enterprise customers.

Attachments I am sharing: redwood_provenance_matrix_v1.xlsx (answers mapped to your rows), pinning-playbook.pdf (overview + ops checklist). If you want a short walkthrough, we can record a 20-minute demo and include the ZIP of artifacts.

We aim to get the ZIP/attestation to you by EOD Wednesday PT; if that's too soon, tell us the date that works.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Solutions — Americas
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_provenance_matrix_v1.xlsx (25KB), pinning-playbook.pdf (220KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pinebridge.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Version backporting, provenance attestations, and pinning workflow

Elena — quick clarifications from product policy (copied below) and noting a small exception for open-license artifacts:

- Training data snapshots: for many open models we provide a declared provenance summary and pointers to upstream data licensing statements; we do not ship full training data snapshots in most cases due to size and licensing constraints. Where a customer requires a data escrow or snapshot for regulatory review, we engage a scoped agreement and escrow process — that is handled under Private deployments.
- Open-license variants: if a model's upstream license imposes attribution or redistribution constraints, our attestation includes the upstream license text and a redistribution summary. We do not modify upstream license terms.

I also attached a short excerpt of our internal pinning playbook that shows the validation checklist and the rollback artifact naming convention (pinning-playbook.pdf). For Pinebridge, if you want the full playbook we recommend a short SOC/Legal workshop so we can map the gaps to your compliance templates.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Policy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pinning-playbook.pdf (excerpt)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pinebridge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Pinebridge RFI Team <rfi@pinebridge.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: Version backporting, provenance attestations, and pinning workflow

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple quick follow-ups:

- Can you confirm the 10-business-day backport SLA applies to CVEs that affect hosted customers as well if they open a support case? Will that require a Dedicated contract?
- Please include the signed attestation PDF in the ZIP you mentioned; we'll ingest that into our evidence repository.

We'd like the 20-minute recorded walkthrough. Can you record something that walks through the ZIP contents (provenance manifest, SHA digests, and attestation) and shows where pin requests live in the console? If possible, include a short note about how you handle open-license attribution in the attestation text.

Replying inline to your earlier message: 

> For an upstream model update (e.g., bug fix, tokenizer change), what is Redwood's policy for offering a backported binary (security/bug fix) for a pinned version?

On that point, we need to understand whether backports can change any behavior that would affect our outputs (e.g., tokenization changes). If you have a semantic-diff process that documents behavior changes, please include it.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll confirm if the SOC/Legal workshop is needed after we see the ZIP/attestation.

Best,
Elena
